title: International Accreditation Bodies
shortDescription: The international cooperation layer that makes an NABL or NABH accreditation mean something beyond India's borders — with one major, very recent structural change.
genZNote: Accreditation bodies get accredited too, in a sense — this is that layer.

sections.heading: Current vs. Historical — A Major Recent Change
sections.body: Until recently, two separate international cooperation bodies existed: the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (ILAC), covering laboratory and inspection accreditation, and the International Accreditation Forum (IAF), covering management-system and product certification accreditation. As of 1 January 2026, these have been brought together into a single new organisation: Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (GACI). Treat ILAC and IAF as HISTORICAL/legacy names for what is now unified under GACI — current material should refer to GACI, while understanding ILAC/IAF for older references.

sections.heading: Regional and Healthcare-Specific Bodies
bullets: APAC (Asia Pacific Accreditation Cooperation) — the regional accreditation cooperation body for laboratory and certification accreditation across the Asia-Pacific region; NABL's regional-level mutual recognition partner.

ISQua (International Society for Quality in Health Care) — operates in a different layer entirely: rather than accrediting individual hospitals, ISQua evaluates and recognises HEALTHCARE ACCREDITATION PROGRAMMES and standards themselves (a form of meta-accreditation). NABH's own standards have gone through this kind of external evaluation against ISQua's guidelines.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: International accreditation cooperation now runs primarily through Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (GACI, formed 1 January 2026 from the earlier ILAC and IAF), alongside regional bodies like APAC and healthcare-specific meta-accreditation via ISQua.
keyFacts: GACI (Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated) formed on 1 January 2026, merging ILAC and IAF.
ILAC (laboratories/inspection) and IAF (management systems/product certification) are now historical/legacy names for what GACI unifies.
APAC is the regional (Asia-Pacific) accreditation cooperation body.
ISQua evaluates healthcare accreditation programmes/standards themselves, not individual hospitals directly.
commonConfusion: An accreditation cooperation body (GACI/APAC) does not itself accredit individual laboratories or hospitals — it creates mutual recognition between NATIONAL accreditation bodies like NABL and NABH.

highYieldFacts: GACI is current (from 1 Jan 2026); ILAC and IAF are historical/legacy names for the two bodies it merged.
ISQua works at the level of accreditation PROGRAMMES, not individual hospitals — a distinct layer from NABH itself.
commonTraps: Citing ILAC or IAF as currently separate, active bodies without noting the GACI merger.
Confusing an accreditation cooperation body with an accreditation body — cooperation bodies don't accredit individual labs/hospitals.
mustRemember: Accreditation body (NABL/NABH) ≠ Accreditation cooperation (GACI/APAC) ≠ Healthcare accreditation organisation (ISQua) — three distinct layers.

confusedTerms.distinction: An accreditation body (NABL, NABH) directly accredits individual laboratories or hospitals. An accreditation cooperation body (GACI, APAC) creates mutual recognition between different countries' accreditation bodies — it doesn't accredit individual labs or hospitals itself.

possibleQuestions: What replaced ILAC and IAF, and when did this change take effect?
How does ISQua's role differ from NABH's role in healthcare accreditation?

questions.prompt: As of 1 January 2026, ILAC and IAF have been brought together into which single organisation?
options: International Society for Quality in Health Care (ISQua)
questions.explanation: GACI was established on 1 January 2026, unifying the earlier work of ILAC and IAF.

questions.prompt: ISQua's role in healthcare accreditation is best described as:
options: Evaluating and recognising healthcare accreditation programmes/standards themselves
questions.explanation: ISQua operates at the meta level — evaluating accreditation programmes and standards, not accrediting individual hospitals directly.
